html:
A Palestinian poet and writer, widely seen as the national poet of the Palestinians. His poems speak of exile, the land, love and loss.

He was born in the village of al-Birweh in Galilee. In 1948, during the Nakba, his family fled to Lebanon, and the village was destroyed. They came back secretly and lived in Israel as Arab citizens. As a young man he joined the Israeli Communist Party, was jailed several times, and became famous for the poem "Identity Card" (1964), with its line "Write down! I am an Arab."

He left in 1970 and lived in Cairo, then in Beirut with the Palestine Liberation Organization, then in Tunis and Paris after the Israeli siege of Beirut in 1982. He wrote the Palestinian Declaration of Independence, read out by Yasser Arafat in 1988. He left the PLO leadership in 1993 in protest at the Oslo Accords.

He settled in Ramallah in the 1990s. His later poetry turned more personal and was read across the Arab world and in many translations. He died in 2008 after heart surgery in the United States and is buried in Ramallah.
sum: A Palestinian poet and writer, widely seen as the national poet of the Palestinians. His poems speak of exile, the land, love and loss.
